page.title: Best Platforms for Virtual Conferences: Buyer Guide
page.description: Compare ten platforms across three cost models, match features to your format, and plan production, rehearsal and follow-up timelines.
page.definition: A virtual conference platform is software that hosts live multi-session events with registration, streaming, networking and analytics, while production covers the crew, run of show and backup stream that make the event run smoothly.
page.quick_answer: Pick a platform tier that matches your session count and attendee capacity, then budget for production separately; rehearse on the real platform two to five days before going live.

sections.h2: What platform type matches my conference format and scale?

blocks.p: Match the platform tier to your session count, attendee capacity and networking needs. Self-serve streaming studios suit single-track webinars up to a few hundred attendees. Mid-market event suites add multi-track agendas, virtual expo booths and matchmaking. Enterprise suites handle thousands of attendees, complex registration paths and deep CRM integration.

ul: Single-track webinar: StreamYard, Livestorm, Zoom Webinars
Multi-track conference: Zoom Events, Hopin, Goldcast, Bizzabo
Enterprise summit with expo: ON24, Cvent, Splash, vFairs

sections.h2: Which cost model fits my budget and buying process?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate the market. Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity let you pay per organiser seat. Self-serve monthly plans let you start without a sales call. Annual contracts quoted by sales unlock enterprise features and dedicated support but require longer commitment.

sections.h2: What engagement and networking features do attendees expect?

blocks.p: Attendees expect live chat, polls, Q&A with upvoting, and one-click networking. Mid-market platforms add virtual lounges, speed networking roulette and AI matchmaking. Enterprise suites layer on gamification leaderboards, sponsor booths with lead capture and attendee-to-attendee video calls. Verify each feature works on mobile browser without app download.

ul: Live chat, polls, Q&A with upvoting — baseline for every tier
Virtual lounges and speed networking — mid-market and up
AI matchmaking and sponsor booth lead capture — enterprise tier
Gamification leaderboards and attendee video calls — enterprise tier

sections.h2: How do I handle recording, replay and follow-up at scale?

blocks.p: Plan for automated cloud recording, on-demand library and CRM handoff before the event starts. Most platforms auto-generate session recordings; enterprise suites add chapter markers, searchable transcripts and branded replay pages. Connect the platform to HubSpot or Salesforce so registrant status updates trigger nurture sequences within twenty-four to forty-eight hours.

ol: Enable cloud recording for every session in platform settings
Set replay expiration or gating rules in the on-demand library
Map registration fields to CRM contact properties
Build nurture workflow keyed to attended, no-show, early-leave tags
Send replay link within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: What production support do I need beyond the software?

blocks.p: The platform is not the production. Someone must own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready. A simple webinar needs one producer. Summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.

Technical check sixty minutes before going live

Edited recording and clips delivered after the event

sections.h2: How do I compare shortlisted platforms side by side?

blocks.p: Score each candidate on capacity, cost model, networking depth, CRM integration, replay features and support SLA. Weight criteria by your must-haves: multi-track agenda, sponsor booths, SSO, dedicated success manager. Run a pilot webinar on the top two before signing an annual contract.

faq.q: How far in advance should I lock the platform for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final so production can build the run of show and schedule rehearsals.

faq.q: What is the typical production budget for a moderated webinar versus a multi-day summit?
faq.a: Moderated webinars range from two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred dollars per production. Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions start at ten thousand dollars and can exceed fifty thousand dollars.

faq.q: Can I use my existing Zoom or Teams licence for a produced event?
faq.a: Yes. Produced events run on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard. The production crew joins as panellists and manages the broadcast from there.

faq.q: What staffing do I need for a virtual summit versus a single webinar?
faq.a: One producer can run a simple webinar. Summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator — four distinct roles — plus a backup stream operator.

faq.q: How quickly should the replay go out after the event ends?
faq.a: Send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours while attendees still remember the event. Automate the hand-off from platform recording to CRM so the nurture sequence triggers without manual upload.
